newsitem.title: THAILAND: Floods stop Thai zinc miner Padaeng work.
newsitem.headline: Floods stop Thai zinc miner Padaeng work.

text.p: Padaeng Industry Plc said on Monday it had suspended zinc mining in Thailand's northern Tak province for two months due to floods and heavy rain.
A company official told Reuters that work at the Tak mine would resume in November.
"The closedown will not affect operation as it is a normal thing we do every year," the official said.
"We normally shut down the mine during September-October as rain and floods make it dangerous to carry on the work," she said.

Padaeng's mine produced 4.1 million metric tonnes of zinc silicate ore in 1995 for its 73,000-tonne-a-year zinc smelter in the same province. Padaeng also imported about 140,000 tonnes of zinc concentrate to feed its smelter.
The company's refinery expansion project is scheduled to be completed by early next year, when its output will be raised to 105,000 tonnes.
"The expansion will be operational on schedule," the official said.
